candidateMetadata.hostNote: Windows desktop; artifacts/executables on D:; own build/test jobs finished before sampling; other user/OS activity not controlled; no power-policy or priority changes. Same input for baseline and candidate; revisions measured in separate serial batches.
candidateMetadata.hostControl: Caller must provide an idle fixed host; this tool does not stop other processes or change power policy
candidateMetadata.wallClock: QPC from immediately before ResumeThread to target exit/timeout observation; includes loader, input, workload and output; not isolated kernel timing
candidateMetadata.cpuClock: GetProcessTimes user/kernel time, converted from 100 ns units; target process only
candidateMetadata.memory: Job Object PeakProcessMemoryUsed: highest per-process peak committed bytes in this sample job (observer excluded); not RSS or allocator live bytes. Benchmark workloads do not spawn subprocesses.
candidateMetadata.compileTiming: One descriptive compile per artifact; process wall includes startup, and MiniC pipeline time excludes JVM startup. No compile-time distribution is claimed.
candidateMetadata.observerWallClock: Java observer process startup and wait; separate from target timing
candidateMetadata.order: Seeded four-row Williams design; every position and directed adjacent pair once per four repetitions
candidateMetadata.instrumentation: none in timing builds; operation-count probes must be reported separately

metadata.order: Seeded Williams four-build order; baseline/candidate adjacent, pair direction alternates by round and build position.
metadata.scope: Process time includes loader, setup, input/output, transfer, ordered full-sequence observation through a volatile function pointer, and erased-tail recreation. No control-time subtraction.
metadata.units: transferredElements counts intended assignments/shifts; observedElements counts hashed data. Neither is a count of generated machine operations.
metadata.metrics: Target QPC wall and GetProcessTimes user/kernel CPU; Job Object PeakProcessMemoryUsed is peak committed bytes, not RSS. Observer excluded. No child workloads.
